data.summary:
Input: A string s.
Output: An integer representing the total number of palindromic substrings in s.
Rules: Substrings that occur at different indices are counted even if their contents are identical.
constraints: s consists of lowercase English letters.

data.generator_code:
import random

def generate(rng, n):
    s = ''.join(rng.choice('abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz') for _ in range(n))
    return [s]

def generate_worst(rng, n):
    s = 'a' * n
    return [s]

data.key_insight: A palindrome mirrors around its center. There are 2n - 1 possible centers for a string of length n (n single-character centers and n - 1 between-character centers). We can expand outwards from each center as long as the characters match and count all valid palindromes.

steps.title: Initialize count
steps.detail: Set a variable total_palindromic_substrings to 0 to keep track of the total number of palindromes found.

steps.title: Iterate through all possible centers
steps.detail: Loop through each index i from 0 to n-1. Each index can act as a center for odd-length palindromes (expand from i, i) and even-length palindromes (expand from i, i+1).

steps.title: Expand and count
steps.detail: For each center, expand outwards while the left and right pointers are within bounds and the characters at both pointers are equal. Increment the count for each valid palindrome found.

steps.title: Return the result
steps.detail: After checking all centers, return total_palindromic_substrings.

data.overview: The Palindromic Substrings algorithm counts how many substrings within a string read the same forward and backward. It does this by treating every possible center (single characters and gaps between characters) as the middle of a potential palindrome and expanding outward while characters match.
data.intuition: Imagine throwing pebbles into a pond at every possible center point. The ripples expand outward as long as the surrounding water forms a symmetrical pattern, counting every valid mirror image you encounter.

flow_nodes.label: Initialize variables
flow_nodes.detail: Set total_palindromic_substrings to 0 and get string length n.

flow_nodes.label: Loop through centers
flow_nodes.detail: Iterate index i from 0 to n - 1.

flow_nodes.label: Expand odd & even
flow_nodes.detail: Call expand_around_center for both single character (i, i) and gap (i, i+1).

flow_nodes.label: Inside expansion loop
flow_nodes.detail: While bounds are valid and characters match, increment count and expand.

pitfalls: Forgetting to check even-length palindromes which center between characters.
Off-by-one errors when expanding left and right indices past the string boundaries.
Confusing the number of distinct palindromes with the total number of palindromic substring occurrences.

events.label: Coach: pattern, brute force and its bottleneck

data.pattern_summary: Expand Around Center involves treating every possible index and space between indices as the center of a potential palindrome, then checking outward expansion. Reach for this when a problem asks to find or count palindromic structures within a sequence.

pattern_options.name: Expand Around Center
pattern_options.feedback: This fits because we can check every possible center point in the string and grow outward to count all valid palindromes.

pattern_options.name: Sliding Window
pattern_options.feedback: Sliding window relies on a contiguous window growing or shrinking based on a condition, but palindromes can expand in both directions from an inner core rather than just sliding along one edge.

pattern_options.name: Two pointers
pattern_options.feedback: While two pointers are used inside the expansion step, the overall strategy requires iterating through all possible centers first, making Expand Around Center the more accurate pattern.

pattern_options.name: Greedy
pattern_options.feedback: Greedy choices make locally optimal decisions to find a global optimum, which does not apply when we need to inspect all possible substring centers.

signals.hint: Implies we need to check many overlapping segments of the string.

signals.phrase: Substrings that occur at different indices are counted
signals.hint: Means identical text at different positions count as separate valid answers.

data.brute_force_idea: Generate every possible substring using nested loops for start and end indices, then check each one to see if it reads the same forwards and backwards.
data.brute_force_why: There are O(n²) possible substrings, and checking if each substring of length k is a palindrome takes O(k) time, resulting in cubic time complexity.
data.bottleneck: Checking if a substring is a palindrome by reversing it re-scans characters that were already part of previously checked substrings.
bottleneck_hints: Look at how many times the inner loop re-evaluates overlapping character ranges.
Notice that checking if 'aba' is a palindrome does not use the fact that 'b' inside it was already known to be a palindrome.
Think about what information carries over when you look at a smaller palindrome inside a larger one.

events.label: Coach: why the complexity is what it is

data.insight: The brute-force solution checks every possible substring and reverses it, resulting in redundant work. The optimized approach treats every character and gap between characters as the center of a potential palindrome, expanding outward until characters mismatch. This removes the need to generate substrings or check them from scratch.

derivation.note: The loop runs for each of the n indices in the string.
The expand function checks up to n characters outward from a single character center.
The expand function checks up to n characters outward from a between-character center.

data.time_summary: The outer loop runs n times. Inside the loop, the expand_around_center helper function takes up to O(n) steps in the worst case. Multiplying the outer loop by the inner work yields an O(n^2) total time complexity.
data.space_summary: The algorithm only uses a few scalar variables (count, left, right, total_palindromic_substrings, n) for tracking indices and counts. Therefore, the extra memory used is O(1).
data.takeaway: When a problem asks to find subarrays or substrings centered around a point, consider checking outward from all possible centers rather than generating all slices.
mistakes: Forgetting to check even-length palindromes by expanding from between two characters (i and i + 1).
Off-by-one errors with index bounds when the left or right pointers go out of string boundaries.
Assuming every expansion takes the full O(n) length when most palindromes terminate early due to mismatches.
